proposal.name: Return sharded sandbox checks within the tool limit

plan.name: Return sharded sandbox checks within the tool limit
plan.summary: Keep the agent's test tool and the factory's checks on the same Sandbox.Run path, with an embedded Python standard-library runner that discovers Test, Fuzz and Example entries, sorts them by package and name and distributes them round-robin among eight concurrent workers, each running its package groups in order, so every discovered top-level test runs in exactly one touched-package shard and new tests join automatically. Keep the offline pinned container, localhost hostname and isolated shared build cache, retain 4 GiB and 1024 process limits per container (12 GiB and 3072 processes for three watcher steps), and limit Go compilation to one package at a time per command with GOMAXPROCS=2. Give the entire Sandbox.Run a ten-minute deadline from entry and each shard an eight-minute timeout, reserve another minute for startup and fifteen seconds for cleanup below both unchanged 900-second backend tool limits, stop the container on deadline, and return package-qualified partial test results and a summary naming passed, failed, still-running and unstarted tests; a failed build, shard, timeout or interrupted run fails the check while independent shards continue, and acceptance tests run afterward with their own package-qualified results under the same deadline. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe these checks, limits and deadline reports, with changed SPEC bullets citing D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0113, D-0117, D-0122, D-0173, D-0189, D-0197 and D-0233 as applicable. This sharding and deadline policy needs a new decision that the merger records, and merger work also includes reloading the watchers and running INVARIANT_PLUMBING_REAL=1 go test ./internal/verify -run '^TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout$' -count=1 -timeout 20m to confirm that three concurrent real-image runs of the checkout, including vet and acceptance tests in internal/verify, pass within the chosen deadline and resource limits.

tests.name: TestSandboxShardsEveryTopLevelTestExactlyOnce
tests.says: Real fixture tests, examples and fuzz seeds run exactly once in the touched-package phase, in eight simultaneous shards assigned by sorted round-robin discovery, with subtests intact, a newly added test included, empty packages allowed, and the chosen container limits enforced; pinned acceptance tests run again afterward.

tests.name: TestSandboxNamesFailuresFromEveryShard
tests.says: An assertion failure, panic, shard timeout or package build error fails the check and names the failed package, test and shard where applicable, while healthy shards and independent acceptance checks still complete.

tests.name: TestSandboxDeadlineReturnsPartialResults
tests.says: The sandbox's own deadline stops hung tests, vet or acceptance checks and removes the container, returning a failed result with completed, failed, running and unstarted tests distinguished and their names retained in the delivered summary.

tests.name: TestSandboxKeepsAcceptanceResultsByPackage
tests.says: Acceptance tests with the same function name in different packages retain their individual outcomes, so another package's passing test cannot satisfy a failing acceptance test.

tests.name: TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout
tests.says: The sandbox deadline, startup reserve and cleanup reserve stay below the tool limits actually configured by every supported backend; an opt-in real-image subtest checks three concurrent cold-cache runs of this checkout, including internal/verify and its pinned acceptance test, finish successfully within that budget.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and five acceptance tests covering sharding, deadlines, failure reporting, resource limits, and documentation updates. The first check passed; real-image validation, decision recording, and watcher reload remain merger work.
